topics.topic: Whether INV-10 tests must explicitly cover repeated JSON member names and at which object levels
questions: Must `test_unreadable_connections_deliver_nothing` explicitly use JSON with a repeated member name—and at which object levels—to demonstrate the newly added rule that a repeated member anywhere breaks the file, or may “a file of another form” be witnessed only by some unrelated schema defect?

Must these tests explicitly use repeated JSON member names—including a repetition inside an unrelated project's nested object—to show the newly added whole-file rejection rule, or may “a file of another form” be witnessed by some other schema defect?

Must the Required tests explicitly show that a repeated member name in the top-level object, the `objects` object, or a connection-entry object makes the whole connections file invalid before project lookup?

quotes:
A missing or extra field, a value of
   another type, a key that is not the canonical spelling of a UUID, or a member name repeated within one JSON
   object anywhere in the file breaks that form. The file is judged whole before any project is looked
   up, so the first condition that applies decides:
- INV-10: nothing is scanned, placed or marked for a project unless the connections file read by that operation is valid and holds a confirmed connection for the project.

For an absent file, a file that cannot be opened, a file that is not UTF-8 or JSON, a file of another form and a record that breaks the form of rule 8, also when that record is unconfirmed or belongs to another project, scan, placement and mark each answer the FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode and write nothing (`test_unreadable_connections_deliver_nothing`), and the service does not start (`test_the_service_does_not_start_with_an_unreadable_connection_record`).
judgement.divergence: One implementer makes the required tests demonstrate repeated member names at the top level, in `objects`, and in an unrelated connection entry; another uses only an unrelated missing-field or wrong-type fixture, so the agent reviewing generated-service evidence sees materially different proof of INV-10.
judgement.why: The Required tests item permits “a file of another form” to be witnessed without exercising the newly specified duplicate-member rule or its whole-file effect.

witness.initial: The connections file contains a confirmed record for project A and a repeated member name inside project B's entry.
events: The caller asks the service to scan project A.
One implementer supplies duplicate-aware fixtures, including the repetition in project B, for the required INV-10 tests.
Another implementer supplies only an unrelated invalid-form fixture for those tests.
outcomes: The required evidence explicitly shows that the whole file is refused with FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE because of the repeated member in an unrelated project.
The required evidence can pass without showing rejection of any repeated member name.
witness.observer: The agent reviewing the generated-service invariant evidence.

topics.topic: Whether INV-02 tests must cover every listed path-segment and metadata failure case
questions: Must the required test exercise every way A3 rule 5 condition 1 can apply, including an absent segment, a failed folder opening, failed metadata, and non-regular objects other than a folder or symbolic link, or only the cases explicitly listed here?

What must the Required tests show for the remaining failures in A3 rule 5 condition 1: an absent or non-folder path segment, a folder-opening failure, an absent last segment, and a failed metadata reading?

quotes: - INV-02: a delivery opens no path that fails condition 1 of A3 rule 5.

Condition 1 is decided from the name, then by opening the photo folder and
   each folder of the name in turn, each in the one before it and without following a link, and by one
   metadata reading of the last segment in the last folder opened, without following a link; the file is
   then opened in that folder, so it is read from the folders that were checked.

topics.topic: Which error takes precedence when an image cannot be opened but declares excessive first-frame dimensions
questions: What failure applies when the image library refuses while opening an image because its declared first-frame dimensions are excessive: `UNREADABLE_IMAGE` because it could not be opened, or `TOO_MANY_PIXELS` because the dimensions exceed the product limit and that check is listed first?

When the library cannot open or decode a source whose header declares a first frame above the pixel limit, does the delivery fail with `too_many_pixels` or `unreadable_image`, and what amount of parsing establishes that a first frame is above the limit?

quotes:
which of them it detects is the library's decision, and a source it cannot open as one of them is
   `unreadable_image`.

Checks run in this order: a first frame above the pixel
   limit (width times height) fails with `too_many_pixels`, a source that cannot be decoded with
   `unreadable_image`, and a result above the Portal's read limit with `too_large`.
judgement.divergence: One passage makes a library open failure `unreadable_image`; the ordered-check passage makes an excessive declared first frame `too_many_pixels`, so the caller and owner can receive different failure reasons for the same source.
judgement.why: A source whose excessive declared dimensions cause the pinned library to refuse opening satisfies both passages, which prescribe different failures without defining how dimensions are established first.
